solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Part of breakfast, say, put in fridge mistakenly

indicators.note: the abbreviation for 'say' is placed inside the rearranged kitchen appliance
letters arranged by mistake are out of their proper order, so the word fridge is jumbled

parts.note: e.g. (for example) is what 'say' means when introducing an instance

explanation.surface: Someone tidies breakfast leftovers into the fridge, getting the shelf wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is not a link word here; it is the abbreviation for 'for example'. 'mistakenly' makes FRIEDG, and 'put in' places the two letters after its E.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg cooked in a pan of fat is a staple of the full cooked breakfast.

clue.text: Source of timber becoming softer with treatment

indicators.note: treated wood is worked on, so the letters of softer are reworked

explanation.surface: Timber gets softer once it has been treated.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodland trees are felled for lumber, so a stand of trees supplies wood.

clue.text: I lifted paintings into extremely nifty container from office

indicators.note: the turned word goes into the outer letters of nifty
extremely means the outermost letters of the word nifty
in a down entry lifted means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: paintings collectively are art

explanation.surface: A thief boasts of hiding pictures in a smart office box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' suits a down entry, where reading upwards turns the word backwards into TRA; 'into' sets it between the outer letters picked by 'extremely'.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-tray is the desk tray holding papers awaiting attention.

clue.text: Steer car out of blasted river

indicators.note: out of signals the letters are taken from within blasted river

explanation.surface: An order to steer a car out of a wretched river.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer a car is to take the wheel and operate the vehicle on the road.

clue.text: Fellow imbibes a small amount of liquid after party, showing sign of stress

indicators.note: to imbibe is to drink in, so the outer word takes the rest inside

parts.note: a gent is a fellow

indicators.note: the small measure follows the party word

parts.note: a rave is a large party
cc, a cubic centimetre, is a tiny measure of liquid

explanation.surface: A man takes a drop of something after a party, looking strained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stress' is the emphasis on a vowel; the grave accent is the backward-leaning mark over letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The grave accent is a diacritic, used in some languages to mark stress or pronunciation.

clue.text: A Conservative chancellor rules over inflation ultimately

parts.note: laws are rules laid down
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word inflation

explanation.surface: A Tory finance minister lays down rules that will eventually tame inflation.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigel Lawson was Chancellor of the Exchequer, Britain's finance minister, under Margaret Thatcher in the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigel Lawson served as Conservative Chancellor of the Exchequer from 1983 to 1989.

clue.text: I say, woman has decapitated nightclub employee

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name

indicators.note: to decapitate is to remove the head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a bouncer guards a nightclub door

explanation.surface: A shocked exclamation that a woman has beheaded a nightclub doorman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I say' is the definition: an announcer is the one who speaks up to tell an audience things.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcaster or presenter who makes announcements is the voice that says what follows.

clue.text: Short of time, celebrity eats fish

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: A star in a rush grabs a fish supper.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardines are small oily fish of the herring family, often sold tinned.

clue.text: Make home around region in part of Asia

indicators.note: the verb for making a home goes around the region word

parts.note: birds nest when they make a home
an area is a region

explanation.surface: Settling down somewhere in a corner of Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Near East covers south-western Asia, the countries nearest Europe.

clue.text: Playwright sounded bad-tempered with most of crew

indicators.note: the clue says the word for bad-tempered is spoken, so its sound gives the start

parts.note: ratty is informal British for irritable

indicators.note: most of the word means all but its final letter is kept

parts.note: a gang is a crew of workers or people

explanation.surface: A dramatist came across as grumpy alongside most of the stage crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounded' gives RATTI, said like RATTY; 'most of' trims GANG to GAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence Rattigan was an English dramatist, author of The Winslow Boy and The Browning Version.

clue.text: Girl producing article — fancy — with end missing

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the last letter of the synonym for fancy is dropped

parts.note: a fancy is an imagined notion, a dream

explanation.surface: A girl writes a fanciful article but leaves off the ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrea is a female given name, so it can stand for a girl in crosswords.

clue.text: Immodest tennis champ overcomes poor player at start of set

indicators.note: one name gets round another, wrapping it entirely like a winner surrounding a defeated opponent

parts.note: Monica Seles won nine Grand Slam singles titles
a ham is a bad, over-the-top actor

indicators.note: at start of points to the opening letter of the word set

explanation.surface: A brazen tennis star beats a weak opponent at the beginning of a set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'player' is an actor here, not a tennis opponent; 'overcomes' wraps the champion's surname around the bad actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without shame behaves brazenly and without modesty, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Care what you'll get from new glasses?

definitions.meaning: care in the sense of overseeing or looking after

definitions.text: what you'll get from new glasses?
definitions.meaning: read as two words, new spectacles give excellent eyesight

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into SUPER VISION, excellent eyesight.
explanation.definitionFit: Supervision is the act of overseeing or watching over something, which is a form of care.

clue.text: Part of kitchen fixed by English couple

definitions.note: the verb sense: to join together

parts.note: a kitchen unit is a fitted cupboard

explanation.surface: A kitchen cupboard was fixed by a pair of English fitters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'couple' looks like two people but is a verb meaning join.
explanation.definitionFit: To couple things is to join or link them, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Travellers returned money after end of trip

indicators.note: the slang for money comes after the selected letter

parts.note: back means returned, as in 'came back'

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the word trip

parts.note: ackers is British slang for money

explanation.surface: Tourists came home with their cash after the trip ended.
explanation.walkthrough: ACKERS is old British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Backpackers are budget travellers who carry their gear on their backs.

clue.text: Outlaw cases compound belonging to church

indicators.note: cases means encloses, so the outlaw word goes around the chemical

parts.note: to ban is to outlaw
silica is silicon dioxide, a chemical compound

explanation.surface: A prohibition encloses a compound owned by a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Basilican relates to a basilica, a type of large early church building.

clue.text: Beef with crust possibly cut by foreign friend

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the last letter is chopped

parts.note: pastry is one kind of crust
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A beef pie with its crust sliced by a friend from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is highly seasoned smoked beef, usually served sliced.

clue.text: Closely followed wild predator

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters run riot

explanation.surface: A wild hunter stalked its prey closely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closely followed' means imitated word for word, not tracked.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeat someone's words mechanically is to imitate them closely, like a talking bird.

clue.text: Arsenal excited, about to try old Newcastle player

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged club name surrounds the legal word
an excited thing is stirred up, so the letters of the club name are agitated

parts.note: to hear a case is to try it in court

explanation.surface: Arsenal supporters get worked up over an old Newcastle striker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' gives ALANSER, and 'about' wraps it round the legal verb. Arsenal and Newcastle United are English football clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Shearer was Newcastle United's record goalscorer and a former England centre-forward.

clue.text: Poor court usher

parts.note: dire means very poor in quality

explanation.surface: A court usher who does the job badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'usher' looks like a noun for a court official; it is the verb, to guide.
explanation.definitionFit: To usher someone is to guide or show them the way.

clue.text: Character in radio series who takes a bow?

definitions.meaning: A long-running BBC radio farming soap
a bowman carries a bow, not an actor bowing

explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC Radio 4 soap opera about a farming family. 'takes a bow' suggests a performer at curtain call, but the bow fires arrows.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowman shoots arrows, and members of the radio family share that surname.

clue.text: Railway in French area going in wrong direction for Austrian region

indicators.note: across the grid a wrong direction is right to left, so the letters run backwards
the railway abbreviation sits inside the name of the French area

parts.note: the Lot is a department in south-western France

explanation.surface: A French regional railway heads the wrong way and ends up in the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives LORYT; 'going in wrong direction' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyrol is a mountainous Alpine state of western Austria.

clue.text: Entering bank, old woman appears more nervous

indicators.note: the word for an old woman goes into the word for a bank

parts.note: a tier is a bank or row of seats
witch is an unkind term for an old woman

explanation.surface: An elderly woman walking into a bank looks increasingly jumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' is a row or tier, not a building where money is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Twitchy describes someone jumpy and on edge; the comparative means more so.

clue.text: Shared first portion taken from pie dish

parts.note: to cut a cake is to share it out

indicators.note: the opening letter is removed

explanation.surface: Slices handed round from a pie dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' is slang for an attractive person, not crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Dish and cutie are both informal words for a good-looking person.

clue.text: Briefly join Khmer leader for raid

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to attach is to join

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A short instruction to team up with the Khmer Rouge chief for a raid.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden assault on a place, and attack covers the same act.

clue.text: His text sent about one's milestone birthday?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the numeral, surrounding it
sent in the sense of sent wild or crazy, so the two words are jumbled

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral; the 's is is

explanation.surface: A man's text message marks a big birthday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent' shuffles HIS TEXT into SIXTETH; 'about' wraps that round I. The question mark flags that a sixtieth is one birthday among several milestones.
explanation.definitionFit: A sixtieth is a round-number anniversary celebrated as a landmark in life.

clue.text: Order tinned nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go mad

explanation.surface: A shopper places an order for tinned nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like the goods being ordered but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An indent is an official order or requisition for goods, a commercial sense.

clue.text: Clever sort in IOW town, with no second name

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the second occurrence of the letter is removed, leaving the first

parts.note: Ventnor is a seaside town on the Isle of Wight

explanation.surface: A bright spark living on the Isle of Wight has no second name.
explanation.walkthrough: VENTNOR has two Ns; 'with no second' drops the later one, giving VENTOR. The Isle of Wight (IOW) is an English island county.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who devises new machines or processes is a clever, ingenious type.
